conflicts: Test-auth helpers are defined four times, incompatibly. PR1 commit 1 adds TestSessions.SignInAsAsync(factory, role, email?, dob?, password?), which mints real sessions through ITokenGenerator. PR2 commit 5 adds TestUsers.CreateAsync(factory, role) through LoginSessionIssuer, which duplicates PR1 and has a different signature. PR3 adds a NEW TestUsers.cs (register via /v1/auth/register plus OTP) that collides with PR2's file, and gets staff tokens from 'TestJwtTokenBuilder perm claims'. PR4 edits TestUsers.cs (SeedActiveCandidateAsync) and also relies on a 'TestJwtTokenBuilder perm variant'. After PR1, TestJwtTokenBuilder tokens carry no sid (TestJwtTokenBuilder.cs:38-42), so they get 401. Consolidate on PR1's TestSessions, add a RegisterViaApiAsync overload there for PR3, and never add perm claims to TestJwtTokenBuilder.

ConcurrencyConflictError is created twice. PR1 commit 3 adds SharedKernel.Domain/Exceptions/ConcurrencyConflictError.cs (409 concurrency_conflict) plus a DomainException(message, inner) ctor. PR2 commit 17 adds SharedKernel.Domain/ConcurrencyConflictError.cs (new), which is the same type at a different path and won't compile next to PR1's. PR3 adds ConcurrentGuardianLinkUpdateError and ConsentConcurrentUpdateError, and PR4 adds InviteStateConflictError, all for the same xmin DbUpdateConcurrencyException case. Reuse PR1's type, or have module-specific codes subclass it. Also extract one shared 'Postgres 23505 on index X' helper into SharedKernel.Infrastructure. Today PR2 (Batch, Guardian UoW), PR3 (Guardian, Consent UoW) and PR4 (Batch, Invite UoW) each hand-roll it.

PageRequest and the SharedKernel.UnitTests project are created twice. PR2's last-but-one commit creates tests/SharedKernel/ExamPlatform.SharedKernel.UnitTests and SharedKernel.Application/Paging/PageRequest with InvalidPageRequestError ('invalid_paging'), default 50, max 200. PR4 commit 1 creates the same project and file with InvalidPagingError, default 25, max 100. Keep PR2's and have PR4 add only PagedResult<T>.

ADR number collision: PR2 writes docs/adr/0002-migrations-and-reference-data-seeding.md and PR4 writes docs/adr/0002-m3-enrollment-scheduling-ownership.md. docs/adr currently holds only 0001-stack.md and template.md. PR4's ADR must be 0003.

Audit handlers will double-write. PR2 adds Application/Audit/{ExamAuthoring,Batch,Invite,Guardian}AuditTrail.cs and registers them with the assembly-scanning AddDomainEventHandlersFrom. PR4 adds NEW Application/Events/{Exam,Batch,Invite}AuditHandlers.cs for ExamPublished, InviteCodeIssued, InviteAccepted and InviteRevoked, which PR2's trails already handle. Two handler classes on the same event means two audit rows. If PR4 also registers its handlers explicitly, the scan registers them a second time and each runs twice. PR4 should extend PR2's trail classes and rely on the scan only.

Guardian work in PR2 is thrown away by PR3. PR2 commits 13 (typed errors plus Guardian.RevokeCandidateLink), 14 (Include CandidateLinks), 18 (UniqueActiveGuardianLink migration with dedupe SQL), 22 (Clock, events, private setters) and 28 (GuardianAuditTrail over GuardianCreated, LinkRequested, LinkRevoked, CandidateUnlinked) all target a model that PR3 commit 5 deletes. PR3 commit 6 then drops and recreates the guardian tables. PR3's file lists also don't delete PR2's GuardianAuditTrail.cs, GuardianAuditTrailTests.cs, GuardianTests.cs, GuardianLinkHandlerTests.cs, the Guardian part of M3AuditTrailTests (GuardianLinkRevoked_IsAudited_WithStaffActor) or PR2's Guardian FakeClock (PR3 marks FakeClock as 'new'). PR3 won't compile unless it removes them. PR2 also says InvalidLinkTokenError is 'kept for PR3', while PR3 deletes it.

Invite code and state logic is implemented twice with different names. PR2 commit 22 does an 8-char CSPRNG code (RandomNumberGenerator.GetString in the domain), InvalidInviteExpiryError for 1..720h, InviteNotPendingError, InviteCodeIssuedEvent, Accept(codeId, actor, now), and the AddInviteRowVersion xmin migration. PR4 does a 10-char IInviteCodeGenerator port, InvalidInviteConfigError for the same 1..720h rule, re-creates InviteNotPendingError and InviteCodeIssuedEvent (listed as new files), and maps xmin again ('shadow uint Version IsRowVersion') in M3InviteCodeHashing. PR4 must build on PR2's types and mapping rather than re-declare them.

Batch member validation and the unique index are done twice, incompatibly. PR2 commit 12 adds InvalidBatchMemberError plus MailAddress/E.164 checks and lower-cases email inside Batch.AddMember(email, phone, actor, now). PR2 commit 18 adds a unique index on (BatchId, Email) WHERE IsDeleted=false, with dedupe SQL and a 23505 translation keyed on that index name. PR4 commit 18 adds a MemberContact value object with InvalidRosterEntryError, re-lowercases emails in SQL, changes AddMember to (name, contact, isMinor, guardian, now) and drops the actor, and creates a partial unique (BatchId, Email) WHERE Email IS NOT NULL AND NOT IsDeleted. That is the same default name, IX_BatchMembers_BatchId_Email, so EF will drop and recreate it, and PR2's 23505 name match needs updating for the new phone index.

Role-claim handling disagrees. PR2's GetPrimaryRole reads ClaimTypes.Role, then 'role'. PR3's risks say the role claim is written as 'role', so RequireRole or ClaimTypes.Role never match. PR4's jwt.ts reads both keys. The code supports PR2 (see wrongAssumptions). PR3's workaround of server-side role checks is fine either way, but its risk note should be corrected so PR4 isn't misled.

Rate-limit policy ownership is inconsistent. PR1 defines Identity-owned consts ('identity-otp-request', etc.) in Identity.Endpoints, configured under 'Identity:RateLimits'. PR3 plans to put 'PR1's OTP policy name' on Guardian endpoints, but under ADR 0001 and PR2's arch rule 6 Guardian.Endpoints cannot reference Identity.Endpoints. PR4 defines an Invite-owned 'invite-accept' policy but binds 'RateLimiting:InviteAccept', which is the Host namespace PR1 uses for RateLimiting:Global. Each module should own its policy and config section: 'Guardian:RateLimits:*' and 'Invite:RateLimits:Accept'.

Dev-only sender pattern diverges. PR1 makes LoggingOtpSender Development-only with OtpDeliveryOptions plus a ValidateOnStart fail-fast validator. PR3's LoggingGuardianVerificationSender is registered in every environment, and its LogCodesInDevelopment flag isn't tied to IHostEnvironment. That repeats the audited NFR-6 defect (IdentityModuleInstaller.cs:39) for guardian codes. Use PR1's Provider plus environment-validator pattern.

Web OTP navigation conflicts. PR1's final web commit moves the destination out of the /verify-otp query string into router state and masks it (NFR-6). PR3's guardian-register navigates to /verify-otp with queryParams {challengeId, purpose, destination, returnUrl}, which re-introduces PII in the URL and bypasses PR1's masked-destination copy.

Claims-helper surface and name. PR2 deletes Identity.Endpoints/ClaimsPrincipalExtensions.cs and adds SharedKernel.Application/Security GetUserId and GetPrimaryRole only. PR1 adds GetSessionId in that deleted file for LogoutHandler. PR3 assumes a HasPermission(code) helper. PR4 calls the helper 'GetRequiredUserId()' and adds HasPermission itself, which is too late for PR3. PR2 must carry over GetSessionId and add HasPermission.

Roster guardian contacts to guardian links has no owner. PR3 says PR4 will add a Guardian.Contracts IGuardianLinkRequests adapter for CSV guardian contacts (FR-50). PR4 explicitly lists 'turning roster guardian contacts into guardian accounts or links' as out of scope. Pick one.

PR3's GuardianEndpoints return Consent.Contracts ConsentRecordDto and ConsentStatusDto straight from POST /v1/guardians/consent and GET /v1/guardians/me/candidates/{id}/consent, which breaks that rule. Map them to Guardian-owned DTOs in Guardian.Application, or explicitly relax the rule in PR2.

PR2 commit 4 deletes Identity.Endpoints/ClaimsPrincipalExtensions.cs, which PR1 extended with GetSessionId() for POST /v1/auth/logout. PR2 must move GetSessionId (reading 'sid', typed 401 on missing) into the shared helper or the solution won't build.

PR3 and PR4 integration tests authenticate staff with TestJwtTokenBuilder perm-claim tokens. Because of PR1's session validation (sid-less tokens get 401), they must use PR1's TestSessions.SignInAsAsync from the start.

PR4's TimeTravelApiFactory (e.g. AcceptByCode_ExpiredCode_Returns410, GetInvite_AllCodesExpired...) conflicts with PR1. SessionValidator uses the injected Clock, so advancing a fake clock past invite expiry (1..720h) marks the 1h test session Expired. And a token minted after advancing gets nbf = the fake time (PR1 sets notBefore = session.IssuedAtUtc), which JwtBearer, running on real time, rejects. PR1's SignInAsAsync needs a sessionLifetime parameter, and PR4's time-travel tests must sign in before advancing the clock.

The exam-builder blank-seriesId 400 (high, exam-builder.ts:160 / ExamAuthoringEndpoints.cs:40) is fixed only in PR4, so the one working authoring UI flow stays broken through PR1-PR3. PR2's seeder commit should add a Development-only, config-driven bootstrap SuperAdmin (email plus password hash from user-secrets). Otherwise the manual verification steps in PR2 and PR4 ('ExamAdmin creates...') cannot be performed.

wrongAssumptions: PR3 (risks): 'JwtSecurityTokenHandler's outbound map writes ClaimTypes.Role as role ... FindFirst(ClaimTypes.Role) probably never matches'. That's wrong. JwtTokenGenerator.cs:34 and :44-51 build a new JwtSecurityToken(claims: ...), and JwtPayload stores each claim under its own Type, so the long ClaimTypes.Role URI is what goes into the token. OutboundClaimTypeMap applies only to the SecurityTokenDescriptor/CreateToken path. With MapInboundClaims=false (Program.cs:32), ClaimTypes.Role therefore matches. PR2's explanation is the correct one. Add a unit test to lock this in.
PR3: 'Consent's private CallerId (ConsentEndpoints.cs:28)'. It is at ConsentEndpoints.cs:40, and PR2 commit 4 already deletes it.

PR3 dependsOn (f) and PR4 dependsOn: 'TestJwtTokenBuilder can emit perm claims (PR2)'. PR2 never does this. It adds TestUsers with real sessions, and PR1 explicitly forbids perm claims on TestJwtTokenBuilder. Its tokens also lack 'sid' (TestJwtTokenBuilder.cs:38-42), so after PR1 they always get 401.

PR4: integration events are 'records deriving from SharedKernel.Domain DomainEvent'. PR2 deletes DomainEvent.cs. Today only M3 events use it, and Identity and Consent events already implement IDomainEvent (UserRegisteredEvent.cs:8), so the type won't exist when PR4 lands.

PR3 dependsOn (a): 'PR1's named policy e.g. otp'. PR1 names its policies identity-otp-request, identity-otp-verify, identity-password-login and identity-password-reset, as consts in Identity.Endpoints. ADR 0001:45 and PR2's rule 6 stop Guardian.Endpoints from referencing them.

PR2 outOfScope: 'Security headers, HSTS, forwarded headers, and OpenAPI/Scalar only in Development ... not assigned to any PR'. PR1 commit 14 covers HSTS, ForwardedHeaders and dev-only OpenAPI/Scalar. Only security headers are actually unassigned.
PR2 outOfScope: 'PR1: ... plus CorrelationId in AssignRoleHandler's audit entry'. PR1's commits never touch AssignRoleHandler.
PR4: seeding batch.read.all means 'one entry' in IdentitySeeder.cs. After PR2 the permission matrix lives in Identity.Domain/Rbac/RbacCatalog.cs, and RbacCatalogTests/RbacSeedingTests assert it.

PR4 risk: the concurrency test depends on the 'public new Guid Id => base.Id' pattern. PR2 also adds the Invite xmin token (AddInviteRowVersion), so PR4 should not map it again.
PR1: 'delete TokenLifetime and DateTime.UtcNow at line 47'. The UtcNow expiry is at JwtTokenGenerator.cs:48 and TokenLifetime at :19. This is trivial, but engineers are told to trust line numbers.
